tagline.value: A 2D puzzle-platformer set in one hotel that exists in more than one era. Switch time and the building changes around you; what you carry doesn't.
tagline.source: itch.io page ('The Astoria Grand Hotel exists in two eras at once… Platforms appear, walls vanish') + crumpyofcl.github.io ('the building changes around them, and nothing they're carrying does')

value.name: Time Switch
value.text: Shift between Present and Past. Platforms appear, walls vanish and hazards change.

value.name: Time Beam
value.text: Freeze objects across both timelines; bounce beams off mirrors to hit targets around corners.

value.name: Box Pull
value.text: Grab and move boxes into position to solve environmental puzzles.

value.name: Dash and Double Jump
value.text: Movement abilities that open paths that were visible but previously unreachable.

structure.value: Progression is gated by abilities, not combat: each new tool opens paths that were visible but previously unreachable. The hotel is interconnected, with hidden rooms and shortcuts.

contributions.source: My previous site (crumpyofcl.github.io). These are my claims — a design doc or code sample is still to be published.
value: The era system — collision layers, object state and physics swapping in step, with a crush check so time closing around the player is a death rather than a glitch.

Procedural puzzle generators with Scene-view grid painting: pipe networks with a connectivity solver, and elemental puzzles that pick their own elements by counting how many valid solutions each set allows.
A save system built around an objective ledger, so a reloaded world remembers which doors are open and which puzzles are done.
An in-build debug console for playtesters — noclip, ability grants, scene jumps and objective control without an editor.

decisions.decision: Treat time closing around the player as a death, not a glitch
decisions.detail: The era system swaps collision layers, object state and physics in step. A crush check catches the moment solid geometry from the other era would occupy the player's space.

why.value: So that time closing around the player reads as a death — a rule of the world — rather than a glitch.
why.source: Paraphrase of crumpyofcl.github.io ('so time closing around the player is a death rather than a glitch')

options.request: Other options considered (e.g. block the switch, push the player out).

evidence.request: What showed this was the right call (playtest, bug report).

decisions.decision: Build saving around an objective ledger
decisions.detail: The save system records objectives, so a reloaded world remembers which doors are open and which puzzles are done.

why.value: So a reloaded world remembers which doors are open and which puzzles are done, not just where the player was standing.

decisions.decision: Put a debug console in the playtest build
decisions.detail: Noclip, ability grants, scene jumps and objective control, available without the Unity editor.

why.value: Playtesters and teammates can reach and repeat any situation without the editor.

decisions.decision: Let elemental puzzles choose their own elements
decisions.detail: The generator counts how many valid solutions each candidate element set allows, and picks from that.
